source.description: Project parser entry that passes the attacker-controlled ODP action string into odp_actions_from_string; LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput is only the harness boundary.

sink.description: MSan crash location where formatted NSH MD2 bytes are read from a buffer containing uninitialized data.

root_cause.description: Padding for parsed NSH MD2 metadata is inserted at the head of the ofpbuf with ofpbuf_push_zeros instead of appended at the tail, so bytes later included in md_size can remain uninitialized.

taint_source.description: The PoC bytes are interpreted by the project as an ODP action string and passed into the OVS action parser.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled md2 hex field is parsed from the ODP action string into a local buffer before being decoded into metadata.

root_cause_analysis.summary: An attacker-controlled ODP action containing push_nsh md2 metadata is parsed into a stack `metadata` buffer. The vulnerable padding code uses ofpbuf_push_zeros(), which prefixes padding instead of appending it after the decoded md2 bytes. The code then trusts `md_size = mdlen + padding` and copies that range through the NSH netlink attribute path. During formatting, ds_put_hex reads bytes from the reconstructed MD2 buffer and MSan observes that part of the range originated from uninitialized stack storage.
root_cause_analysis.why_patch_works: The developer patch bounds the parsed md2 hex length, uses the actual `metadata` array size for the ofpbuf stub, changes the padding operation from ofpbuf_push_zeros() to ofpbuf_put_zeros(), and zero-initializes the reconstructed nsh_hdr before copying attributes. These changes ensure that the byte range described by md_size is initialized before it can be copied and formatted.

origin_context.description: MSan reports the uninitialized value was created by allocation of stack variable `metadata` in this frame.
